question: Which version of Windows introduced the Start menu?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Windows 95**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Windows 95** was the first version of the Windows operating system to introduce the Start menu, a revolutionary feature for navigation.
 
• The Start menu combined the list of installed programs with quick access to system settings, making it user-friendly and efficient.
 
• It was launched on **August 24, 1995**, and marked a significant shift towards graphical user interfaces (GUI).
 
• The Start button, located at the bottom-left corner of the screen, became a hallmark of Windows operating systems.
 
• This version also introduced other innovations like the taskbar, long file names, and built-in support for plug-and-play hardware.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Windows Operating System:**

 
 
• Windows is a family of operating systems developed by Microsoft, designed for personal computers, tablets, and embedded systems.
 
• It is one of the most widely used operating systems globally, with billions of active installations.
 
 
 
• **Graphical User Interface (GUI):**
 
 
• The GUI allows users to interact with electronic devices through visual indicators like icons and buttons instead of text-based interfaces.
 
• Windows 95 was a major step forward in popularizing GUI for mainstream computer users.
 
 
 
• **Taskbar:**
 
 
• The taskbar, introduced in Windows 95, allows users to see and switch between open applications easily.
 
• It is located at the bottom of the screen and includes the Start button, quick launch icons, and the system clock.
 
 
 
• **Plug and Play (PnP):**
 
 
• Windows 95 introduced built-in support for PnP, allowing hardware devices to be automatically recognized and configured by the operating system.
 
• This feature greatly simplified the process of adding new hardware to a computer.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Start Menu:**
 
 
• The Start menu became an iconic feature of Windows, evolving through subsequent versions like Windows XP, Windows 7, and Windows 10.
 
• It remains a central element for accessing applications and settings in modern Windows systems.
